note: Original places, batch 3 of 4: wild habitats for the fauna of the continent. Each is a Location under a wild or city, linked to the animals found there. Written for Asetheria; no third-party text.

entries.name: The Leopard's Ledge
entries.summary: A cold rock shelf on Kharveth where a pale cat hunts goats at dusk and a bone-eating vulture drops its meals on the stones.
entries.body:
A broad, cold shelf of broken rock high on Kharveth, above the line where the shepherds will take their flocks. Goat tracks cross it in the morning, and the bones at the foot of the cliff say what happens to the goats by night.

## Who lives here

The shelf is the hunting-ground of a [[Plateau Rock-Leopard]], and the [[Bone-Breaker]] circles above it, dropping what the cat leaves onto the rocks below to crack the marrow.

## Visiting

Shepherds leave a goat on the ledge each winter as a toll. A hunter who wants the pelt is told that the leopard has never been seen by a man who came looking.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the toll goat was taken early this year, and a child went missing the same night. The village suspects the cat; the tracks say otherwise.

entries.name: The Lion Grass
entries.summary: A golden stretch of steppe where the manes of the great cats and the antlers of the strange antelope show above the grass at dawn.
entries.body:
A broad golden stretch of the steppe where the grass grows shoulder-high and the herds of the horse-peoples avoid grazing in the evenings. At dawn the manes of the great cats rise above the stems like banners, and the ground is stamped with the prints of a thousand hooves.

## Who lives here

The grass is the range of the [[Mane-King of the Steppe]], the hunting-ground of the odd-nosed [[Malaunian Saiga]] herds, and the winter pasture of the shaggy [[Two-Hump Camel]].

## Visiting

The horse-peoples will guide a traveller across for a gift of salt. They will not guide him back.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a herd of saiga has moved west, as if fleeing something. The horse-peoples have not said what.

entries.name: The Aurochs Glades
entries.summary: A chain of green clearings deep in the old forest where huge wild cattle graze under the eye of bears and the old hunters' ghosts.
entries.body:
A chain of green clearings deep in the forest, each a mile across and joined by trails that the great beasts wear into the ground. The glades have no villages, no roads and no signs, and the hunters who know them keep their knowledge to themselves.

## Who lives here

The glades are the home of the [[Great Forest Bull]] and the shaggy [[Hill Bison]], and the dark edges are the den-country of the [[Mountain Brown Bear]].

## Visiting

A hunter needs a licence from the forest-wardens and a guide from the tribe. A second-hand tale of a glade is not a licence.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: someone has been killing the bulls and taking only the horns. The wardens suspect a buyer in the capital.

entries.name: The Onager Plain
entries.summary: A flat red plain where wild asses run faster than horses, and the lizards and jackals wait for what the sun leaves.
entries.body:
A wide, flat, stony plain in the desert where the only shade is a rock and the only water is a well that moves. The wild asses graze at dawn and dusk and run at the sight of a rider, faster than any horse and with a stamina that makes the royal hunters swear.

## Who lives here

The plain is the range of the [[Wild Ass of the Waste]], and the [[Gold-Coat Jackal]] follows the herds. In the cracks live the [[Sand Monitor]] and the buried [[Horned Sand-Viper]].

## Visiting

The royal hunt crosses the plain once a year. A traveller who meets it is invited to join, and does not refuse.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the well moves because the ground is shifting. The nomads say something is rising under the plain.

entries.name: The Horse Meadows
entries.summary: A rolling green plain where the sweating, golden horses of the king are bred and the wolves keep the herds honest.
entries.body:
A rolling green plain where the king's horse-breeders run their herds, and where the grass is said to grow in the shape of the wind that blew a week ago. The horses are slim, long-legged and golden-coated, and a foal sells for a village. The wolves come down from the hills each winter, and the herders keep their fires burning.

## Who lives here

The meadows are the pastures of the [[Heavenly Horse]], the range of the [[Plateau Wolf]] and the winter ground of the [[Hill Fallow Deer]].

## Visiting

The breeders welcome buyers in spring. A buyer who wants to see the best stud is told to wait, and is kept waiting.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a mare has foaled something with a scar like a brand. The breeders have not told the king.

entries.name: The Boar Thicket
entries.summary: A dense hillside scrub where a tusked beast the size of a pony is hunted by heroes, and tortoises carry the old lyres' shells.
entries.body:
A dense, thorny scrub on the Oros foothills, impassable except by the tracks the boars cut and the tunnels the partridges use. Hunters go in with spears and dogs and come out with stories, a few of which are true.

## Who lives here

The thicket belongs to the [[Tusker of the Thicket]], the slow [[Hill Tortoise]], and the running [[Rock-Partridge]] that flushes in a burst when the dogs come near.

## Visiting

The village at the thicket's edge hosts a hunt each autumn and feeds the hunters, living and dead.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the old boar of the stories has been seen again. A hunter who shot at it found his arrow gone and his hand marked.

entries.name: The Ibex Crags
entries.summary: Sheer grey cliffs where wild goats stand on ledges no hunter can reach and a great eagle rides the wind above them.
entries.body:
A set of sheer grey cliffs on the Cloudspine ridge, ledged and fissured in a way that only a goat could love. The animals stand motionless on the edges, and the eagle that rides the updrafts above them has a nest on a pinnacle the soldiers have named after a general.

## Who lives here

The crags are the home of the [[Cliff-Goat]], the [[Horned Wild Sheep]] on the lower terraces and the [[King's Eagle]] above them.

## Visiting

The ridge forts will let a hunter pass for a share of the meat. The eagle, they say, takes a share of the hunter.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the eagle's nest holds something that glitters. The soldiers have been arguing over who gets to look.

entries.name: The Hyena Hollows
entries.summary: A set of low, bone-white dens in the black stone where the laughter at night is the only sound for ten miles.
entries.body:
A set of low hollows in the base of the black ridge, strewn with bone and bleached by the sun. The dens are used by the same families for generations, and at night the laughter carries across the plain, to the discomfort of every caravan camped within earshot.

## Who lives here

The hollows belong to the [[Grave-Laugher]], with the [[Giant Eagle-Owl]] nesting on the ridge above and the [[Fat-Tail Scorpion]] in the cracks below.

## Visiting

Caravans camp elsewhere. A traveller who has no choice is advised to sleep with a fire and a friend.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the hyenas dig at one spot every night. The caravaners say a body is buried there that wants out.

entries.name: The Hunting Park
entries.summary: A walled royal game reserve outside the frontier fortress, where trained cheetahs, falcons and lynxes are flown at hares for the garrison's sport.
entries.body:
A walled reserve of scrub and meadow outside the frontier fortress, kept by the garrison for the sport of its officers. The huntsmen train cheetahs to run at hares from the backs of horses, and falcons to take birds from the sky, and the lynxes are kept in cages for display.

## Who lives here

The park's kennels and mews hold the [[Acheaorian Hunting Cheetah]], the [[Hunting Falcon]] and the tufted [[King's Lynx]].

## Visiting

Officers' guests are welcome. A commoner who wants to see a cheetah run must befriend a huntsman.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a cheetah has been freed from its cage and has not been recovered. Three people have blamed three different men.

entries.name: The Pelican Islands
entries.summary: Reed islets in the great marsh where pelicans, pheasants and cranes nest and the sturgeon run beneath them.
entries.body:
A cluster of floating reed islets in the heart of the marsh, anchored to nothing and moving a few yards each year. The birds nest by the thousand, the fishermen punt among them, and in the deep channels beneath, the great fish run in spring.

## Who lives here

The islets are the nesting-ground of the [[Bill-Bag Pelican]], the [[Phasian Pheasant]] and the [[Grey Crane]] in winter. In the channels swim the [[Black-Egg Sturgeon]], and in the still pools the [[Healer's Leech]].

## Visiting

A fisherman's guild runs punts to the islets. A day's trip costs a day's wage and a promise not to take eggs.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: one islet has anchored itself to something. The fishermen say it is a hand.

entries.name: The Flamingo Lagoons
entries.summary: Salt-pink shallows on the inland sea where a million pale birds stand in the water and the sunset makes the whole lagoon blush.
entries.body:
A string of shallow, salt-pink lagoons on the shore of the inland sea, shimmering with algae and shrimp. At dusk the birds stand in thousands and the whole surface turns the colour of embers, and on windless evenings the effect is so complete that sailors have steered towards it by mistake.

## Who lives here

The lagoons are the feeding-ground of the [[Flame-Wader]]. A herder's hut at the southern end serves tea and tells tourists nothing they do not already know.

## Visiting

A traveller may watch from the shore. Wading in is forbidden, and the herders enforce it with sticks.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the lagoons have begun to turn grey. The herders blame a spring that has changed, and the hunters blame the herders.

entries.name: The Petrel Stacks
entries.summary: Rock pillars in the strait where storm-birds nest and the water below is thick with ink-fish, snail and eel.
entries.body:
A group of tall rock pillars rising from the strait, white with guano and shrieking with birds. The wind is made here, the sailors say, and the petrels that nest on the stacks are the first to flee when a storm is coming. The water at their feet is rich with life.

## Who lives here

The stacks are the nesting-ground of the [[Aeolian Petrel]]; the rocks below hold [[Purple-Snail]], the shallows [[Ink-Fish]] and the crevices [[Pond-Moray]].

## Visiting

Boats pass by but do not land. A sailor who has seen the petrels leave knows to turn for harbour.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the petrels left a week early. The harbour-master says there is no storm. The sailors disagree.

entries.name: The Sponge Banks
entries.summary: Clear, rocky shallows off the foggy coast where free-divers cut sponge and coral and net the red fish that die in colours.
entries.body:
A broad shelf of clear, rocky water just inside the sea-fog, where the free-divers of the coast work from open boats. A diver goes down on a stone with a knife and a net, cuts what he can in a breath and is hauled up with his lungs on fire. Their widows keep the nearest tavern.

## Who lives here

The banks hold the [[Diver's Sponge]] and the [[Blood-Coral]] of the sea-caves, and the sandy fringe is the net-ground for the [[Dying Mullet]].

## Visiting

The divers' guild sells a day on a boat. A visitor who wants to dive is advised to think again.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a diver came up with a coral branch that was not red but black, and has been unable to say what he saw below.

entries.name: The Kingfisher Reach
entries.summary: A calm green stretch of the founding river where blue birds dive and the winter is gentle for a week each year.
entries.body:
A quiet reach of the Tiberius between two bridges, its banks of soft earth pitted with burrows. The water is green and slow, the willows trail in it, and a bird of impossible blue flashes along it at dawn. In midwinter there is a week of dead calm that the villagers call by the bird's name.

## Who lives here

The reach is the home of the [[Halcyon]]. A fisherman's family has lived on the bank for ten generations and will tell any visitor which burrows are occupied.

## Visiting

The reach is public. Fishing is not, and the bailiffs patrol on market days.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the calm has not come this winter. The fishermen say the birds have left, and no one has seen where.

entries.name: The Crocodile Pool
entries.summary: A garlanded pool beside the royal canal where a sacred river-beast is fed by priests and watched by the white birds.
entries.body:
A broad pool beside the old royal canal, lined with steps and garlanded with flowers, where a huge river-beast lies half in the water and is fed by priests with fish and wine-soaked bread. The birds that stand about the pool pick food from its teeth, and the priests say the god and the bird have made a covenant.

## Who lives here

The pool is the home of the [[River-Dragon]] and the attendant [[The Watching Ibis]], a long-billed white bird that the priests regard as a clerk of the god.

## Visiting

The priests admit pilgrims at dawn. A visitor who drops anything in the pool is advised to leave it.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the beast is ill, and the priests have not told the town. If it dies, a younger, wilder one will come.

entries.name: The Vulture Crags
entries.summary: White-streaked cliffs above the gorge where the great scavengers wheel and the sky-burial towers wait for their dead.
entries.body:
White-streaked cliffs above the gorge, riddled with nests and ringed by wheeling birds from dawn until the thermals fail. The people of the plateau lay their dead on the towers at the cliff's foot and let the birds do the rest, and a priest of the rite lives in a hut by the stair.

## Who lives here

The crags are the roost of the [[Sky-Cleaner]]. A priest of the rite will answer questions about the birds, and none about the dead.

## Visiting

The stair is open to mourners. A traveller who wants to see the birds is directed to a viewing ledge a half-mile off.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a body was taken from the tower, not by the birds. The priest has not reported it.

entries.name: The Cobra Heaps
entries.summary: Rubble mounds outside the caravan city where the snakes sun themselves, the mongooses patrol and the charmers ply their trade.
entries.body:
A series of old rubble mounds outside the caravan city's east gate, where the demolition of a dozen forgotten buildings left cracks and hollows that the snakes were happy to move into. A guild of charmers has rights to the ground and the locals know to give the heaps a wide berth.

## Who lives here

The heaps are the den of the [[Hood-Asp]], watched by the mongoose called the [[Snake-Warden]], which the charmers keep as a working partner.

## Visiting

A charmer will give a demonstration for a few coins. The guild does not allow strangers to handle the snakes.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a snake of a colour no charmer recognises has been seen on the heaps. The guild has locked the gate.

entries.name: The Mulberry Sheds
entries.summary: Rows of warm, whispering sheds where silkmoths eat mulberry leaves all day and the whole building sounds like rain.
entries.body:
A row of long wooden sheds behind the caravan city's silk-quarter, warm and humid and thick with the sound of ten thousand mouths chewing leaves. The caterpillars are fed four times a day by women who sleep in the sheds during the feeding season, and the cocoons are stifled in steam before the moths can break out.

## Who lives here

The sheds house the [[Tabrishi'ir Silkmoth]], bred for a pale, strong thread that a merchant house will not export in raw form.

## Visiting

The house does not admit strangers to the sheds. A merchant who wants to buy is received in the front room and offered tea.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the house's best breeder is selling eggs to a competitor. The penalty, by old custom, is the loss of both hands.

entries.name: The Qanat Pools
entries.summary: Cool, dark reservoirs at the mouths of the underground channels, where blind newts swim and nightingales sing in the garden above.
entries.body:
A series of stone-lined pools at the mouths of the underground channels that bring water to the garden city. The water is cold and clear, the walls are green with moss, and the air smells of wet stone. The channel-keepers are a hereditary guild with their own saints and their own jokes.

## Who lives here

The pools are the home of the pale [[Qanat Newt]], and the garden above them is where the [[Night-Singer]] sings at dusk.

## Visiting

A channel-keeper will lead a visitor down to the first pool. Beyond it, the way is not for the casual.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the channels flow in a direction they did not last year. A keeper says the water is being pulled.

entries.name: The Geese Court
entries.summary: A white-paved court on the capital's hill where the sacred geese are kept, the swans glide on a royal pond and the dormice are fattened for feasts.
entries.body:
A paved court on the capital's holiest hill, attached to the temple of the queen of heaven. The sacred geese are kept in a long pen along one wall, fed from the temple's own stores, and credited with having once saved the city by waking the guards. A royal pond at the court's far end holds swans, and a row of clay jars along the kitchen wall holds fattening dormice.

## Who lives here

The court is the home of [[The Geese of Juno]], the [[Silent Swan]] on the pond and the [[Banquet Dormouse]] in the kitchens.

## Visiting

The court is open on feast days. A visitor who is rude to a goose is treated as a visitor who has been rude to the goddess.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: the geese have fallen silent. The priestess says it means nothing, and has doubled the watch.

entries.name: The Torpedo Shallows
entries.summary: A sandy bay where the fishermen step carefully, because the flat grey fish in the sand deliver a blow like a hammer.
entries.body:
A broad, sandy bay on the strait, its bottom so flat and pale that a swimmer can see the shadows of fish. The fishermen shuffle their feet as they wade, because the sand is home to a flat, grey, round fish that delivers a numbing shock when it is trodden on. Some men take it as a cure for headaches and some as a warning.

## Who lives here

The bay is the home of [[The Numbfish]]. The physicians of the coast pay for live ones, and the fishermen for a wage that matches the pain.

## Visiting

The bay is open to all. A visitor who wades barefoot is warned once.
entries.dmNotes: Hook: a fisherman's dead body was found in the shallows, unmarked and smiling. The coroner says it was the fish; the coroner is being paid.
